### When Towers Fall
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/when-towers-fall
Passage: Luke 13:4-5
Points:
- When sudden tragedies strike, people often assume that victims suffered because of their own exceptional wickedness.
- Jesus rejected the idea that victims of violence or falling towers were worse sinners than their neighbors.
- While suffering exists because humanity is fallen, earthly calamity does not correspond directly to individual guilt.
- Catastrophes serve as urgent warnings that all sinners deserve judgment and must examine their own hearts.
- Rather than questioning why bad things happen, people should marvel at God's daily mercy and repent.

### What Would Jesus Say?
Author: Michael A. Youssef
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/leading-the-way/leading-the-way-devotional-for-september-7-2026.html
Passage: Luke 13:1-5
Points:
- Sudden disasters naturally lead people to question where God is and why He allows suffering.
- Jesus corrected the mistaken assumption that people killed in tragedies were guilty of greater sin.
- Tragedies demonstrate human fragility and serve as a sober warning of coming judgment.
- Instead of judging others, every person must recognize their need to repent before God.
- God mercifully provides a way of escape and eternal life through faith in Jesus Christ.
